title: He Who Began a Good Work
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Our debt is already canceled, and the one who started the work in us promises to finish it.
exhortation: We were justified in a moment, once for all. It is done. Our record of sin and the debt we owed has been wiped away. We don't have to work to pay off a debt or be on good enough behavior to get off probation. It's a finished work by Jesus Christ on the cross.

Isn't it wonderful that our process of sanctification doesn't start with a huge mountain of debt? Sometimes we look at our lives, see the long road ahead and all the work that needs to be done, and get discouraged. But we forget that the work was started by wiping clean all the debt we had racked up.

And here's how the Bible's logic works. It says that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion. So the canceling of our debt is proof that he will finish the work. Thank you, Lord, that he will finish the work.

How would you feel if you had a billion dollars in debt, and someone canceled it all and then gave you a great, high-paying job? I think we'd be ready to get to work. You just went from "I'll never get out of this" to everything you do putting you more and more into the positive.

I'm not here today to figure out how that works, how we work out our salvation and yet Christ is doing it for us. I just know that we're called to work, and that the work we're called to do is a good work and a joyful one. I think that's one of the reasons Jesus can say his yoke is easy and his burden is light: he first took the mountain of debt off our shoulders.

So as we wrap up, we should see the work of sanctification as an exciting and joyful work, because Jesus has canceled our debt and promises to see us to the end. Is the sanctification process feeling burdensome to you? It might be that you're carrying burdens from your past that you aren't meant to carry. Don't take up the burdens Jesus has already removed. And remember that the one who started it will be the one who finishes it.
prayer: Lord, I pray that we would live in the reality of your finished work. When you said those words, as you bore the agony of the cross, the torture, the whips, the scourging, the burden of the cross, the mockery, the wrath of God poured out on you, you took it all, and then you said, "It is finished."

I pray that we would believe you, Lord. Give us faith to trust you completely. Whatever hold the enemy might have in our lives, whatever lie tells us this truth is not the truth, Lord, let us trust in you fully and completely. Thank you, Lord. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.
